In 2024, the latest year available, about **12.8%** of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty. That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM, 2023 base), Canada's official poverty line.

- Source: Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015 (percentage of persons under 18 in low income, Alberta). It was released 2026-04-29.
- Trend: the rate was 11.9% in 2023, 12.0% in 2022, 8.1% in 2021 and 4.6% in 2020. The 2020 and 2021 figures were lower, likely reflecting pandemic income supports.
- Alternative measure: on the Low Income Measure after tax (LIM-AT), the 2024 rate was **13.9%** (v96520326, same table).

The two measures differ in method, so the rates are not directly comparable.

In 2025, employees in Alberta's public administration earned an average of **$46.96 per hour** and **$1,773.90 per week**. These figures cover full- and part-time employees of all genders, aged 15 and over.

| Year | Average hourly wage | Average weekly wage |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | $46.96 | $1,773.90 |
| 2024 | $46.10 | $1,732.50 |
| 2023 | $44.82 | $1,703.37 |

- **Sources:** Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0064-01, Employee wages by industry, annual. The hourly series is v2292826 and the weekly series is v2292827. The reference period is 2025, released 2026-01-09. Values are in current dollars.
- **Limitation:** The NAICS "Public administration" category covers federal, provincial and local governments. I couldn't find a table that isolates Alberta's provincial government alone. These figures are therefore for all public administration in Alberta, not only the provincial level.

The average total income of people aged 15 and over in Alberta was **$66,100 in 2024**. That is the latest year available, and the figure is in 2024 constant dollars. It averages only over people who reported income, so zeros are excluded.

- It was $66,300 in 2023 and $66,000 in 2022.
- Over 2013–2024 the yearly figures ranged from $65,600 to $72,700.

Source: Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0239-01, vector v107680657. The series is Alberta; 15 years and over; total gender; total income; average income (excluding zeros). It was released 2026-04-29.

This is an average, which is pulled up by high earners. For a typical person, use the median instead. It is available in the same table (statistic 5) but I didn't retrieve it.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024, the latest year available. The figure is in 2024 constant dollars.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0190-01, vector v96414571. The series is "Alberta; Median total income; Economic families and persons not in an economic family". It was released 2026-04-29.
- **Caveat:** This table measures income per economic family or unattached person, not per household, so it is the closest official match to "household income".
- **Recent years:** The median was $98,400 in 2023 and $96,700 in 2022, in 2024 constant dollars.

In 2024, **12.8%** of Alberta children under 18 were living in poverty. That uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), Canada's official poverty line.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015. Reference period is 2024, released 2026-04-29.
- **Alternative measure:** The Low income measure after tax (LIM-AT) gives 13.9% for 2024 (vector v96520326, same table).
- **Trend (MBM):** The rate was 11.9% in 2023, 12.0% in 2022, 8.1% in 2021 and 4.6% in 2020. The 2020 and 2021 figures are low, and Statistics Canada's status codes on those years (6 and 7) differ from 2022–2024. I haven't checked what those codes mean.

Average weekly earnings for all employees in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912, including overtime) are **$1,883.03 for August 2026**. That is the latest month available.

- **Latest month:** $1,883.03 in August 2026. The monthly figures are not seasonally adjusted. Source: Statistics Canada table 14-10-0203-01, vector v1560358. The August figure is from the 2026-10-29 release.
- **Recent months:** $1,877.58 in July 2026 and $1,877.87 in June 2026. The 12-month average from September 2025 to August 2026 is about $1,835.
- **Latest annual figure:** $1,702.65 for 2025. This is about $1,703 a week, or roughly $88,500 a year if annualized across 52 weeks. Source: table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415.

These are average weekly earnings in current dollars from the Survey of Employment, Payroll and Hours. The tables don't give a separate hourly wage for this group, so I haven't reported one.

The average total income of individuals in Alberta was **$63,200** in 2024, the latest year available. The figure is in 2024 constant dollars.

- Source: Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0091-01, vector v1529672282. The series is "Alberta; All persons; Total – Gender; Total income; Average income". It was released 2026-04-29.
- The median is much lower at **$45,500**, because a few high earners pull the average up. Source: same table, vector v1529672284.
- The average was $63,900 in 2023 and $63,400 in 2022 (same vector, same constant dollars).

This covers all persons, which is people with or without income. I did not pull the "excluding zeros" average, which would be higher.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024. That is the latest year available, in 2024 constant dollars.

- **What it measures:** This is the median for economic families and persons not in an economic family, which is Statistics Canada's closest measure to household income. It is not strictly "household" income.
- **Recent trend:** It was $98,400 in 2023 and $96,700 in 2022.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0237-01, vector v107654786. The reference period is 2024, and the table was released 2026-04-29.

In 2024, **12.8%** of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty. That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line, with the 2023 base.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015. The reference period is 2024 and the data were released 2026-04-29.
- **Trend:** The rate was 11.9% in 2023 and 12.0% in 2022. It was 8.1% in 2021 and 4.6% in 2020, a low that came in the pandemic-benefit years.
- **Other measure:** On the after-tax Low Income Measure (LIM), the 2024 rate is 13.9% (vector v96520326, same table).

Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration workers averaged **$1,883.03 per week** in August 2026. That figure covers all employees and includes overtime. It is the latest month available, and the data are not seasonally adjusted.

- **Recent months:** July 2026 was $1,877.58, June $1,877.87, May $1,869.42 and April $1,849.30.
- **Past 12 months:** the monthly average from August 2025 to August 2026 was about $1,824, ranging from $1,694.36 to $1,883.03.
- **Industry definition:** this is the "Provincial and territorial public administration" industry. It is not the same as all public-sector workers, since teachers and health workers are classified elsewhere.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0203-01, vector v1560358 (Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours), released 2026-10-29. Values are in current dollars.

I did not retrieve hourly wages or annual wages for this industry. The annual table 14-10-0064-01 doesn't break out provincial public administration; it only has a broader "Public administration" category.

The average total income of individuals in Alberta was **$63,200** in 2024, the latest year available. That figure is in 2024 constant dollars and covers all persons and both genders.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0091-01, vector v1529672282. It was released 2026-04-29.
- **Recent trend:** The average was $63,900 in 2023 and $63,400 in 2022. Over 2013–2024 it ranged from $63,200 to $71,000.
- **Median:** The median total income was $45,500 in 2024 (vector v1529672284). It is well below the average, so a minority of high earners pulls the average up.

The average counts everyone, including people with zero income. The table also has an "excluding zeros" version, which I didn't pull.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024, in 2024 constant dollars. After tax, it was **$85,300**.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0237-01. The vectors are v107654786 for total income and v107654846 for after-tax income. The reference period is 2024, released 2026-04-29.
- **Unit of measure:** The table covers "economic families and persons not in an economic family". That is close to the usual idea of a household, but it isn't the same thing. I didn't find a table that reports it strictly by household.
- **Trend:** The median total income was $98,400 in 2023 and $96,700 in 2022. The 2013–2024 range was $96,600 to $108,300.
